result:
The city hired a man to remove unnecessary signs.

At first, the work was easy. He took down NO SWIMMING beside a fountain that had been dry for twenty years. He removed TEMPORARILY CLOSED from the door of a demolished cinema. In a municipal basement, he found a sign reading THIS SIGN MUST REMAIN VISIBLE and, after some consideration, turned it toward the wall.

His supervisor praised his judgment.

By November, the obvious work was finished. The man began taking longer walks.

Outside a bakery, he discovered a handwritten notice:

**PLEASE DO NOT TAP ON THE GLASS.  
THE BREAD CANNOT HEAR YOU.**

He went inside.

“Is this necessary?” he asked.

“Absolutely,” said the baker.

He left it alone.

At the railway station, he removed a faded instruction telling passengers to have their tickets ready. Tickets had been digital for years. Behind the sign was a small rectangle of brighter paint, and behind that, when a maintenance worker scraped it, an older instruction:

**WRITE WHEN YOU ARRIVE.**

This was not railway policy. Someone had painted it directly onto the wall.

The man stood looking at it through the departure of three trains.

Then he called his supervisor.

“Does an instruction become unnecessary,” he asked, “if nobody can enforce it?”

“Usually,” said his supervisor. “Why?”

“No reason.”

He covered the words with a piece of cardboard until he could decide what to do.

That evening, he called his sister. They had not quarreled; they had simply become people who intended to call each other.

“Did you need something?” she asked.

“No,” he said. Then, because this sounded alarming: “I found something at work.”

He told her about the wall. She remembered their father making them telephone from a booth outside the coach station, even though home was only a ten-minute walk away.

“He wanted time to put the kettle on,” she said.

The next morning, the man returned with a small brush and a tin of paint matched to the old lettering. He touched up the W, which the scraper had damaged, and removed the cardboard.

On his work sheet, under *Action taken*, he wrote:

**None. Sign still in use.**
